meta_description: Coding Unicorns — a lightweight, fast IDE built in Rust, inspired by VSCode. 30 to 80 MB of RAM, extended through plugins.
tagline: A lightweight, fast IDE, built in Rust.
lead: Inspired by VSCode, without the weight. The editor is deliberately bare: no language is hard-coded — syntax highlighting, LSP and developer tools all come from installable extensions.
platforms_line: Windows · Linux · macOS (Apple Silicon) — automatic updates
figures:
• 30–80 MBof RAM targeted, versus 300–500 MB for VSCode
  • 0hard-coded languages: everything comes from extensions
  • 43configurable keyboard shortcuts
  • 3platforms: Windows, Linux and macOS
download_intro: Pick the file for your system. Once installed, Coding Unicorns updates itself: it checks for a new version at startup and verifies every download against its SHA-256 checksum.
download_tip: Linux / macOS: make the binary executable with chmod +x coding-unicorns-*, then run it. Windows: the .msi installer is recommended; the .exe is a portable build that needs no installation.
features:
• ✏️ Editor

    • Undo/redo, selection, word wrap
    • Side-by-side split editor Ctrl+\
    • Multi-cursor Ctrl+D Ctrl+Shift+L
    • Code folding and bracket matching
    • Auto-closing brackets and quotes

  • 🧭 Navigation

    • Command palette Ctrl+P Ctrl+Shift+P
    • File tree with icons and inline rename
    • Breadcrumbs with the current symbol
    • Go to Definition F12, back/forward Alt+←/→
    • Workspace search and Find & Replace with regex

  • 🌿 Git

    • Current branch, ahead/behind and commit graph
    • Create, rename, merge and delete branches
    • Stage/unstage, commit, push, pull, stash
    • 3-pane merge tool for conflicts
    • Per-line git blame and gutter diff

  • 💡 LSP

    • Hover, completion, find references
    • Rename symbol, code actions, signature help
    • Document formatting
    • Inline diagnostics: errors and warnings

  • 🖥️ Terminal & Debug

    • Built-in terminal: real PTY, multiple tabs, 256 colors
    • DAP debugging: breakpoints, step over/into/out
    • Call stack and variables
    • Launch configurations launch.toml

  • ⚙️ Configuration

    • Dark, Light, Monokai, Solarized Dark, One Dark themes and custom colors
    • 43 shortcuts to set in Settings → Keybindings
    • Optional auto-save
    • Automatic updates verified with SHA-256
extensions_intro: Each extension is a Rust crate compiled as a cdylib and described by a manifest.toml. It brings syntax highlighting and hover for its languages and names the language server to start; the IDE installs that server's dependencies (npm, pip, cargo, go, dotnet) for you. 14 official modules: Rust, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Python, Go, Vue, Svelte, HTML, XML, TOML, C#, PowerShell and speedster-js.
extensions_steps:
• Open the Extensions panelfrom the activity bar (puzzle icon).
  • Browse the registryand search for a language under “Browse registry”.
  • Installa build made for your system, checked with SHA-256 — no Rust toolchain needed.
extensions_more: Updates show up in the same panel (“Update to …”), and uninstalling can also remove the language server's dependencies. Extensions can also be installed from a Git repository, a ZIP archive, a local folder or a Cargo workspace. Prebuilt modules are available for Windows x86_64, Linux x86_64 and macOS Apple Silicon.
